title: Ruy Lopez: Noah's Ark trap
line: Black's pawns chase the queen and then trap White's bishop.

steps.text: The Ruy Lopez. Black guards the pawn on e5 with another pawn.
Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares, to attack the pawn on e5. It is one choice here.

also.e1g1: Castling is the move masters play most here, also sound. This lesson pushes the pawn.
also.c2c3: That is also sound and often played. This lesson pushes the pawn.

steps.text: The pawns chase your bishop. Step it back to b3, where it still aims at f7.
Take the knight that jumped into the center, so it cannot hit your pieces from there.
The pawn on d4 looks free. If the queen takes it, as club players very often do, the pawns chase her and the last one traps the bishop.
Back before the trap: leave the pawn on d4 for now. Push the pawn on c2 to open lines instead.

wrong.d1d4: That is the trap you just saw: the pawns chase the queen, and the bishop is shut in.

also.b3d5: Moving the bishop off the trap first is also sound. This lesson pushes the pawn.
also.a2a4: Hitting the pawns on the queen side is also sound. This lesson pushes the pawn.

steps.text: Take back with the knight. You are a pawn down, but your pieces come out fast and the bishop is free.
steps.after: White has open lines and quick play for the pawn. The bishop on b3 is out of danger.

summary: A pawn on the edge of a long pawn chain can trap a bishop. Before taking a pawn, check what the pawns do next.
